Rashi on Yevamot 35a:10:1.hebrew: אם היו כהנות - בנות כהנים, ואפילו נשואות לישראל, דלא מהני האי זנות לאסרן לבעליהן:
Rashi on Yevamot 35a:10:1.english: If they were kohanot - Daughters of priests, and even [if] married to an Israelite, for this act of licentiousness is not effective to forbid them to their husbands.

Rashi on Yevamot 35a:10:2.hebrew: נפסלו מתרומה דבי נשייהו - שאם ימות בעלה וזרע אין לה, אינה שבה אל בית אביה כנעוריה, דפסיל לה האי זנות, כדתניא לקמן באלמנה לכהן גדול (יבמות דף סח.): כהנת, לויה וישראלית שבא עליה גר עמוני כו', ויליף טעמא מובת כהן כי תהיה לאיש זר — כיון שנבעלה לפסול לה, פסלה. ואע"ג דמותבינן: ואימא נבעלה לפסול חייבי כריתות, ומשנינן: "כי תהיה" כתיב, הנך דאית בהו הוייה — אלמא זנות דחייבי כריתות לא פסיל מאכילת תרומה — הא הדר מייתינא התם קרא אחרינא: "כי תהיה אלמנה וגרושה", למעוטי כותי ועבד שאין לו אלמנות וגירושין בה, ומההוא קרא נמי נפקא לן חייבי כריתות, דהא אין לו אלמנות וגירושין בה. ומעיקרא פרכינן הכי: ואימא חייבי כריתות ולא חייבי לאוין:
Rashi on Yevamot 35a:10:2.english: They are disqualified from the teruma of their fathers' households - [meaning] that if her husband dies and she has no children, she does not return to her father's house as in her youth, for this forbidden intercourse disqualifies her; as it is taught in a baraita later in [the chapter entitled] "A Widow to a High Priest" (Yevamot 68a): "A daughter of a priest, a daughter of a Levite, or a daughter of an Israelite with whom an Ammonite convert had intercourse, etc." And [the baraita] derives the reason from [the verse], "And if a priest's daughter be [married] to a strange man" [Leviticus 22:12] — once she has had intercourse with one who is unfit for her, she is disqualified. And even though we raise an objection [there]: "Say [that the verse refers to] one who had intercourse with one unfit [for her due to] prohibitions punishable by karet," and we answer: "be [tihyeh]" is written, [referring to] those with whom there is valid betrothal [havayah] — thus, forbidden intercourse of prohibitions punishable by karet does not disqualify [her] from eating teruma — nevertheless, we subsequently cite another verse there: "when she is a widow or divorced" [Leviticus 22:13], to exclude a Cuthean [gentile] and a slave, with whom she has no [status of] widowhood or divorce; and from that verse we also derive [disqualification from] prohibitions punishable by karet, for with him she has no [status of] widowhood or divorce. And originally we asked thus: "Say [that it disqualifies in the case of] prohibitions punishable by karet, and not [mere] negative prohibitions."

Rashi on Yevamot 35a:1:1.english: And the Sages decreed [for] a minor, etc. - And regarding a minor female convert, they did not decree, because it is not common.

Rashi on Yevamot 35a:2:1.hebrew: מכלל דהואי - בתמיה. וכי מעשה כזה אירע בימי חכמים? והא "שנים שקידשו" קתני, ולא תני מעשה:
Rashi on Yevamot 35a:2:1.english: By inference that there was [such an occurrence] - [This is asked] in astonishment: did such an incident occur in the days of the Sages? But [the Mishnah] teaches, "Two who betrothed," and does not teach an [actual] incident!

Rashi on Yevamot 35a:2:2.hebrew: אלא כהוראת שעה היתה - ולא היתה, דלא גזרינן בה. מ"ט? חילוף לא שכיח:
Rashi on Yevamot 35a:2:2.english: Rather, it was like a provisional edict - and it did not [actually] happen, for we do not issue a decree in that [case]. What is [the] reason? Switching is uncommon.

Rashi on Yevamot 35a:3:1.hebrew: חוץ מגיורת ומשוחררת גדולה - מדקתני בהאי חוץ גדולה, מכלל דצריכות להמתין דקאמר בגדולות קמיירי:
Rashi on Yevamot 35a:3:1.english: Except for a female convert and a freed maidservant [who is] an adult - Since in this "except" [clause] it teaches "an adult," it follows by implication that [when] it says "they must wait," it is speaking of adult women.

Rashi on Yevamot 35a:4:1.english: A female convert and an adult emancipated [maidservant], for whom promiscuity is common, let [the Sages] issue a decree - that they should wait in order to distinguish between seed sown not in sanctity and seed sown in sanctity.

Rashi on Yevamot 35a:4:2.hebrew: הוא דאמר כרבי יוסי - דלא גזר, כדמפרש טעמא דאשה מזנה מתהפכת כדי שלא תתעבר. ומיהו בישראלית גזר שמואל זנות אטו נשואין שמתעברת, ולא סבר כר' יוסי דלא גזר בהו כדאמר לקמן באנוסה ומפותה. אבל בגיורת לא גזור זנות שבנכרית משום נשואין דבנכרית, דאפילו גיורת נשואה, כיון דדעתה לאיגיורי, מתהפכת נמי כדי להבחין בין זרע קדושה לזרע שלא בקדושה, כדלקמן:
Rashi on Yevamot 35a:4:2.english: He stated [his ruling] in accordance with Rabbi Yosei - Who did not issue a decree, as [the Gemara] explains the reason: that a woman who engages in promiscuous intercourse turns over so as not to become impregnated. However, in the case of a Jewish woman, Shmuel did issue a decree [regarding] promiscuous intercourse on account of marriage, [in] which she becomes impregnated, and he does not hold like Rabbi Yosei, who did not issue a decree in their [case], as [the Gemara] says below regarding a raped woman and a seduced woman. But in the case of a female convert, they did not issue a decree [regarding] promiscuous intercourse during [her] gentile state on account of marriage during [her] gentile state, for even a married convert, since her intention is to convert, also turns over in order to distinguish between seed [conceived in] sanctity and seed [conceived] not in sanctity, as [stated] below.

Rashi on Yevamot 35a:5:1.english: She guards herself - And she carries absorbent wool with her, and it is ready for her.

Rashi on Yevamot 35a:5:2.hebrew: אלא יוצאה בשן ועין - דלא הות ידעת מעיקרא דעתידה להשתחרר, לא מיטרחא ומזדהרא לאתויי מוך בהדה:
Rashi on Yevamot 35a:5:2.english: But [a maidservant] who goes free through [the loss of] a tooth or an eye - Since she did not know beforehand that she was going to be freed, she does not trouble herself and take care to bring mokh [an absorbent plug] with her.

Rashi on Yevamot 35a:6:1.hebrew: אנוסה ומפותה - ישראלית, והרי אונס ממילא הוא ואין לה מוך:
Rashi on Yevamot 35a:6:1.english: A woman who was raped and a woman who was seduced - [This refers to] an Israelite woman; and behold, rape [occurs] by itself, and she does not have a mokh [absorbent wad].

Rashi on Yevamot 35a:7:1.hebrew: מתהפכת - ואף יוצאה בשן ועין נמי ליכא השתא למפרך, דכיון דהיפוך קל הוא לה ואין בו טורח, מתהפכת היא, דכל אשה מזנה אינה רוצה להתעבר:
Rashi on Yevamot 35a:7:1.english: Turns over - And even [the case of a maidservant] who goes free through [loss of] a tooth or an eye can also not be raised as an objection now, for since turning over is easy for her and there is no trouble in it, she turns over, for every promiscuous woman does not want to become pregnant.

Rashi on Yevamot 35a:8:2.hebrew: ישראלית לא - בתמיה. הואיל ואשת כהן היא, אפילו בת ישראל נמי אסורה לבעלה כהן:
Rashi on Yevamot 35a:8:2.english: [An] Israelite woman, no? - [This is asked] in astonishment: since she is the wife of a priest, even the daughter of an Israelite is also forbidden to her husband, [who is] a priest.

Rashi on Yevamot 35a:8:3.hebrew: נשי כהנים - אם בעליהן כהנים, נפסלו להן, דאשת כהן שנאנסה אסורה לבעלה:
Rashi on Yevamot 35a:8:3.english: Wives of priests - If their husbands are priests, they become disqualified to them, for the wife of a priest who was raped is forbidden to her husband.

Rashi on Yevamot 35a:8:4.hebrew: נשי ישראלים לא - בתמיה. וכי אם בעליהם של אלו ישראלים, מי לא מיפסלו נמי לכהונה, שאם ימותו אלו לא ינשאו לכהנים:
Rashi on Yevamot 35a:8:4.english: The wives of Israelites, no - [This is said] in astonishment: If the husbands of these [women] are Israelites, are they not also disqualified from [marrying into] the priesthood, so that if these [husbands] die, [the women] may not marry priests?

Rashi on Yevamot 35a:9:1.hebrew: והאמר רב עמרם כו' ואנהרינהו לעיינין ממתניתין - כלומר, הביא לנו ראיה ממשנתנו. ואותה משנה לקמן בהבא על יבמתו (יבמות דף נו.):
Rashi on Yevamot 35a:9:1.english: But didn't Rav Amram say, etc., and he lit our eyes from the Mishnah - That is to say, he brought us a proof from our Mishnah. And that Mishnah [is] later in [the chapter] Haba Al Yevimto (Yevamot 56a).

Rashi on Yevamot 35a:9:2.hebrew: אשת ישראל שנאנסה אף על פי שמותרת לבעלה - מוהיא לא נתפשה (במדבר ה), הא נתפשה מותרת; אפ"ה פסולה לכהונה אם ימות בעלה:
Rashi on Yevamot 35a:9:2.english: The wife of an Israelite who was raped, even though she is permitted to her husband - [This is derived] from [the verse] "and she was not seized" (Numbers 5[:13]) — [implying that if] she was seized, she is permitted [to her husband]; even so, she is disqualified from the priesthood if her husband dies.

Tosafot on Yevamot 35a:3:1.hebrew: חוץ מגיורת ושפחה משוחררת גדולה - והא דתניא בהחולץ (לקמן יבמות דף מב.): "לפיכך גר וגיורת צריכין להמתין שלשה חדשים" — כר' יהודה אתיא, דחייש שמא לא נתהפכה יפה יפה. א"נ, אפילו כרבי יוסי, וה"ק: "לפיכך גר וגיורת צריכין להמתין" — אם ידוע שנבעלה ולא נתהפכה. ועוד אר"י, דיש לחלק, דלא מינטרא נפשה כלל כשמתגיירת עם בעלה, כיון שכל הזרע מאותו איש, ואין חוששת להבחין בין זרע שנזרע מבעלה זה בקדושה לשלא נזרע בקדושה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 35a:3:1.english: Except for a female convert and an adult freed maidservant - And that which is taught in [the chapter] HaCholetz (below, Yevamot 42a): "Therefore, a male convert and a female convert must wait three months" — [that baraita] accords with Rabbi Yehudah, who is concerned that perhaps she did not turn over thoroughly enough [after intercourse to prevent conception]. Alternatively, [it accords] even with Rabbi Yose, and this is what it is saying: "Therefore, a male convert and a female convert must wait" — [that applies] if it is known that she had intercourse and did not turn over. Furthermore, Rabbi Yitzchak said that one can distinguish [between the cases], for she does not guard herself at all when she converts together with her husband, since all the seed is from that same man, and she is not concerned to distinguish between seed that was sown by this husband in sanctity and [seed] that was not sown in sanctity:

Tosafot on Yevamot 35a:4:1.hebrew: גיורת ומשוחררת דשכיחא לגזור - פירוש: לגזור שיהיו צריכות להמתין, ולא לגזור אטו בת ישראל קאמר, דמהא לא הוה משני מידי:
Tosafot on Yevamot 35a:4:1.english: A female convert and a freed maidservant, where [promiscuity] is common [among them], let [the Sages] issue a decree - Explanation: [this means] to decree that they must wait [three months], and it does not mean to decree [upon them] on account of a Jewish woman, for from this [statement of Rabbi Yosei, the Gemara] would not have answered anything.

Tosafot on Yevamot 35a:7:1.hebrew: אשה מזנה מתהפכת - וכן גיורת ומשוחררת, כיון דדעתה לאיגיורי; אבל יוצאה בשן ועין, מודה בה רבי יוסי:
Tosafot on Yevamot 35a:7:1.english: A woman who engages in promiscuous intercourse turns over - And likewise a female convert and a freed maidservant [do so], since she intends to convert; however, [with regard to a maidservant who] goes free through [the loss of] a tooth or an eye, Rabbi Yose concedes regarding her.

Tosafot on Yevamot 35a:8:1.hebrew: כהנות אין ישראלית לא - ובכתובות (דף נא.), גבי הא דתנן "ובכהנת אהדרינתיך למדינתיך", לא דייק הכי, אלא דוקא הכא — משום דכי משני "אימא נשי כהנים", אכתי אית ליה פירכא אחריתי: "נשי כהנים אין, נשי ישראלים לא":
Tosafot on Yevamot 35a:8:1.english: Daughters of priests, yes; an Israelite woman, no - And in Ketubot (51a), regarding that which we learned in the Mishnah: "And [if she is] a priest's wife, I will return you to your province," [the Gemara] does not make such an inference, rather specifically here [it does so], because when it answers, "Say: wives of priests," it still has another objection: "Wives of priests, yes; wives of Israelites, no?!"

Tosafot on Yevamot 35a:9:1.hebrew: אע"פ שמותרת לבעלה פסולה לכהונה - פי' בקונט' טעמא דשמעתין משום "ובת כהן כי תהיה לאיש זר". ולר"י נראה דמבת איש כהן לא שמעינן אשת איש וכל חייבי כריתות הנאסרות ע"י קדושין, משום דלא הוי זר אצלה מעיקרא. והכי משמע בהבא על יבמתו (לקמן יבמות דף נו:), דקאמר רבא: אשת כהן שנאנסה ובא עליה, לוקה משום זונה ומשום טומאה; ואי מ"בת כהן כי תהיה לאיש זר" שמעינן נמי אשת איש, א"כ יהא לוקה נמי מהאי קרא, דלכהונה נמי אסורות מק"ו דלקמן בפרק אלמנה (יבמות דף סח: ושם) — דלא חשיב לה התם אזהרה מן הדין, אלא גילוי מלתא בעלמא הוא. וה"נ משמע כן קצת מדקאמר: "אף על פי שמותרת לבעלה פסולה לכהונה". ואי פסולה מקרא דבת כהן, פשיטא דאין לחלק בין אונס לרצון. ואי היא גופה אתא לאשמועינן, דשייך קרא דבת כהן בחייבי כריתות דע"י קדושין כיון דשייך בהו ממזרות, אע"ג דלא הוי זר אצלה מעיקרא — אם כן לישמעינן הכי בהדיא, וממילא ידענו דלא שייך בהאי קרא לפלוגי בין אונס לרצון באשת איש טפי מבשאר [פסולי כהונה]. אלא לר"י נראה דפסולה מן הכהונה מטעם טומאה וזונה, כדאמר בהבא על יבמתו (לקמן יבמות דף נו: ושם); וללישנא דאמר התם דכל באונס לא מיקריא זונה, פסולה לכהונה משום טומאה גרידא. ומיהו קשה לר"י: כיון דלא כתיב טומאה אאשת ישראל שנבעלה באונס — דכתיב "והיא לא נתפשה", הא נתפשה מותרת — אם כן אמאי פסולה לכהונה? דבכלל איסור טומאה הוי בעל ובועל ותרומה וגם כהונה, וכי שרי לבעלה תשתרי נמי לכהונה. ואמר ר"י דההוא קרא ד"לא נתפשה" לא מיירי אלא בטומאה דבעל גרידא; ד"נטמאה" קמא אית לן לאוקמי לבעל, ולענין בעל שרי אונס בישראל. אבל "ונטמאה" בתרא, דנפקא לן מינה איסור תרומה וכהונה, לא מפליג בה בין אונס לרצון, בין אשת כהן לאשת ישראל, ויש לאסור בכל ענין; דכיון דאשכחן באשת כהן דאפילו באונס אסורה, אין לנו לחלק בין אונס לרצון לענין תרומה וכהונה אפילו באשת ישראל. ומיהו גבי בועל, אע"ג דלא כתיב ביה "לא נתפשה", יש לחלק בין אונס לרצון באשת ישראל, דסברא הוא דלא נאסרה על הבועל אלא כשנאסרה על הבעל. ולפי פר"י, אין פסולה זונה לתרומה מקרא דבת כהן, אלא שמא מטעם דכלליה קרא בהדי חללה פסולה לתרומה כמו חללה. ובפרק החולץ (לקמן יבמות דף מד: ד"ה הכא) כתב ר"י מזה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 35a:9:1.english: Although she is permitted to her husband, she is disqualified from the priesthood - Rashi explained the reason of our sugya [as being] because of [the verse], "And a priest's daughter who is [married] to a stranger." But it appears to Ri that from "a priest's daughter" (bat ish kohen) we do not derive a married woman or all those liable to karet who become forbidden through betrothal (kiddushin), because he was not a "stranger" to her initially. And so it is implied in [the chapter] Haba Al Yevimto (below, Yevamot 56b), where Rava says: [If] the wife of a priest was raped and [her husband] cohabited with her, he receives lashes on account of [cohabiting with] a zonah and on account of defilement (tumah); and if from "And a priest's daughter who is [married] to a stranger" we also derive a married woman, if so, he should also receive lashes from this verse — for they are also forbidden to the priesthood via the kal vachomer [stated] below in Perek Almanah (Yevamot 68b and there), where it is not reckoned as a prohibition derived by logic (azharah min hadin), but rather it is merely a disclosure of the matter (gilui milta). And this is also somewhat implied from [the Gemara's] saying, "Although she is permitted to her husband, she is disqualified from the priesthood." For if she is disqualified from the verse of "a priest's daughter," it is obvious that there is no distinction between coercion and willingness. And if it came to teach us this very point — that the verse of "a priest's daughter" applies to those liable to karet [forbidden] through kiddushin, since mamzerut applies to them, even though he was not a "stranger" to her initially — if so, let it teach us this explicitly, and we would automatically know that it is not relevant in this verse to distinguish between coercion and willingness regarding a married woman any more than regarding other [women disqualified from the priesthood]. Rather, it appears to Ri that she is disqualified from the priesthood on account of defilement (tumah) and zonah, as [the Gemara] says in Haba Al Yevimto (below, Yevamot 56b and there); and according to the version that says there that anything [done] under coercion is not called a zonah, she is disqualified from the priesthood on account of defilement alone. However, it is difficult for Ri: Since defilement is not written regarding an Israelite's wife who was cohabited with under coercion — as it is written, "and she was not seized" (lo nitpasah), [implying that if] she was seized, she is permitted — if so, why is she disqualified from the priesthood? For included in the prohibition of defilement are the husband, the adulterer, terumah, and also the priesthood; and since she is permitted to her husband, she should also be permitted to the priesthood. And Ri answered that that verse of "she was not seized" speaks only of defilement regarding the husband alone: for the first [mention of] "she was defiled" (nitma'ah) we must establish as referring to the husband, and with respect to the husband, coercion is permitted in [the case of] an Israelite. However, [regarding] the latter [mention of] "and she was defiled" (venitma'ah), from which we derive the prohibition of terumah and the priesthood, it does not distinguish therein between coercion and willingness, [nor] between a priest's wife and an Israelite's wife, and one must forbid [her] in every case; for since we find regarding a priest's wife that even under coercion she is forbidden, we must not distinguish between coercion and willingness with respect to terumah and the priesthood even for an Israelite's wife. However, regarding the adulterer, even though "she was not seized" is not written regarding him, one should distinguish between coercion and willingness for an Israelite's wife, for it is logical that she is not forbidden to the adulterer except when she is forbidden to the husband. And according to Ri's explanation, a zonah is not disqualified from terumah from the verse of "a priest's daughter," but rather perhaps because the verse included her together with a chalalah, [so] she is disqualified from terumah just like a chalalah. And in Perek HaCholetz (below, Yevamot 44b, s.v. Hakha) Ri wrote about this.
